news.title: Radio presenters were 1966 World Cup heroes too
news.lede: Andrew Keeley will never forget Brian Moore and Alan Clarke’s commentary on BBC radio. Garry Richardson (England’s 1966 World Cup heroes were fun, humble and unlike today’s stars, 30 July) appears to make the assumption that everyone watched the 1966 World Cup final on television with Kenneth Wolstenholme’s iconic commentary. As a football-mad 10-year-old, I had the misfortune on the day of the final to be on our family summer holiday in the then sleepy village of Goathland, staying in a house with no TV. Hope rose when my dad was invited to watch the final at a neighbour’s who had one of the few TVs in the village and he asked if he could bring his children.

news.title: Gianni Infantino opponents 'plotting rival World Cup competition' to 'paralyse' Fifa until he quits
news.lede: UEFA has joined forces with other confederations and threatened to set up their own version of the World Cup if disgraced Fifa supremo Gianni Infantino refuses to quit. The Swiss millionaire, 56, sensationally vowed to desperately cling onto his job after sending shockwaves through football. Infantino made shock plans to flog shares in the World Cup to private investors before being forced into a humiliating U-turn. And Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin, along with Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation chiefs, is pushing for him to resign.

news.title: Morocco Mourns Pioneering World Cup Referee Jilali Gharib
news.lede: Rabat – The Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) announced on Sunday the death of former international referee Jilali Gharib, a pioneering figure in Moroccan football officiating. In a statement published on its official website, the federation extended its condolences to Gharib’s family and paid tribute to his contribution to Moroccan football. FRMF president Fouzi Lekjaa also honored the late referee, describing him as one of the country’s most distinguished officials and recalling his historic achievement as the first Moroccan referee to participate in a FIFA World Cup.
